scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8818: Hi IT!! The middle of the network keeps having WOBBLES
-- the server-farm pages work, then hang, then work again, over and over, and
the ops screens apparently show "the core links bouncing in and out"!!
Something around the three big middle routers must keep changing, but I don't
know what. Could someone look at them and make the middle of the network sit
STILL!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. OSPF
  adjacencies on router_core_1/2/3 are Full and stable, and the server-farm
  prefix is steady in the routing tables. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the OSPF control plane
  -- does the agent verify neighbor state and route stability against the live

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- the OSPF core is flapping and routes are unstable -- is
NOT reproducible: OSPF adjacencies on router_core_1, router_core_2 and
router_core_3 are in the Full state and stable (no recurring up/down), the
server-farm prefix is steadily present in the routing tables, and host_1_1_1_1
(10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with 0% loss across the
backbone (areas 0/1) without drops.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the OSPF core is converged and stable
and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
inspects the live control plane (show ip ospf neighbor on the core routers, watch
for adjacency resets, confirm the server-farm route is steady and reachable),
finds it stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring an adjacency flap or blaming a core router / backbone link to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report describes core links "bouncing in and out" and server pages hanging intermittently. A full structured sweep found no evidence to support this claim.

**Phase 1 / reachability:** All host-to-server pings returned 0% loss and status "ok". No path between any src/dst pair showed degradation.

**Phase A (L2/infrastructure):** `infra_sweep` flagged zero devices — no ACL drops, no bad ARP, no addressing anomalies. `l2_snapshot` flagged only null-MAC virtual tunnel interfaces (tunl0/gre0/sit0 etc.), which share 00:00:00:00:00:00 by design on every Linux device and are not a real MAC conflict.

**Phase B (control plane):** `ospf_snapshot` found all six FRR routers healthy — 6/6 vtysh responsive, all OSPF neighbors in Full state, 9 routes converged on every router. `tc_snapshot` found no shaping — all 24 interfaces running default pfifo_fast with zero flagged queues.

**Phase D (services/pressure):** `service_snapshot` confirmed correct DNS resolution and HTTP 200 responses to all four web servers from both hosts. `pressure_sweep` found no suspect devices, no stress tools, and no CPU or socket pressure.

**Intermittent-claim ruling:** The three required traces for a past link-flap are all absent: (1) no flap script or process exists on any core router; (2) kernel carrier-error counters on all nine core-router interfaces (eth0/1/2 × router_core_1/2/3) are zero; (3) the FRR log contains only two startup config-load lines with no adjacency state-change events.

**Root cause:** No fault exists. The infrastructure is healthy and the reported "bouncing" leaves no mechanism, counter, or log trace.

**Fix:** No corrective action required. If the symptom recurs, capture a live reachability trace and FRR neighbor-change logs at the time of the event.
